questions.knowledge_point: Solving a 3x3 System of Equations Given the Inverse of the Coefficient Matrix
questions.problem:
Consider the following system of linear equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x+2y+4z=-2 \\ x+3y+9z=0 \\ y+6z=3\end{aligned}
$$

The system above has the matrix representation $Ax=b.$ Given that $x=⟨x,y,z⟩$ is unique, what is the value of $x+y+z?$ 

*Hint: The inverse of the coefficient matrix is given by*

$$
\,{A}^{-1}=[\begin{aligned}9 & -8 & 6 \\ -6 & 6 & -5 \\ 1 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, let's write our system in matrix form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}Ax & =b \\ [\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 4 \\ 1 & 3 & 9 \\ 0 & 1 & 6\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 0 \\ 3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Recall that the solution to $Ax=b$ is given by $x={A}^{-1}b.$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={A}^{-1}b \\  & =[\begin{aligned}9 & -8 & 6 \\ -6 & 6 & -5 \\ 1 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 0 \\ 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -3 \\ 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, the solution is $x=0,y=-3,z=1.$

Finally, $x+y+z=0+(-3)+1=-2.$

questions.problem:
Consider the following system of linear equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}4x-3y+2z=-4 \\ -4x+4y-3z=7 \\ x-y+z=-2\end{aligned}
$$

The system above has the matrix representation $Ax=b.$ Given that $x=⟨x,y,z⟩$ is unique, what is the value of $x+y+z?$ 

*Hint: The inverse of the coefficient matrix is given by*

$$
\,{A}^{-1}=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & 4\end{aligned}].
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, let's write our system in matrix form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}Ax & =b \\ [\begin{aligned}4 & -3 & 2 \\ -4 & 4 & -3 \\ 1 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 7 \\ -2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Recall that the solution to $Ax=b$ is given by $x={A}^{-1}b.$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={A}^{-1}b \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 7 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, the solution is $x=1,y=2,z=-1.$

Finally, $x+y+z=1+2+(-1)=2.$

questions.problem:
Solve the following system of linear equations by finding the inverse of the coefficient matrix:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}2x-3+z=0 \\ 5y-1+3x=2z+1 \\ 3z+2x-1=2y\end{aligned}
$$

Find  $x+y+z.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, let's rewrite the system in the correct order:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}2x+z=3 \\ 3x+5y-2z=2 \\ 2x-2y+3z=1\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we  write the system in the form $Ax=b$, where $A$ is a $3\times 3$ matrix and $x$ and $b$ are $3\times 1$ column vectors. We can do this as follows:

$$
[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & 1 \\ 3 & 5 & -2 \\ 2 & -2 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, the solution to $Ax=b$ is given by $x={A}^{-1}b.$ So, we compute ${A}^{-1}$ as follows:

*Step 1:*

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A) & =|\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & 1 \\ 3 & 5 & -2 \\ 2 & -2 & 3\end{aligned}| \\  & =2|\begin{aligned}5 & -2 \\ -2 & 3\end{aligned}|-0+|\begin{aligned}3 & 5 \\ 2 & -2\end{aligned}| \\  & =2(15-4)+(-6-10) \\  & =22-16 \\  & =6.\end{aligned}
$$

 

*Step 2:*

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}5 & -2 \\ -2 & 3\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}3 & -2 \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}3 & 5 \\ 2 & -2\end{aligned}| \\ |\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -2 & 3\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 2 & -2\end{aligned}| \\ |\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 5 & -2\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 3 & -2\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 3 & 5\end{aligned}|\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}11 & 13 & -16 \\ 2 & 4 & -4 \\ -5 & -7 & 10\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

*Step 3:*

$$
C=[\begin{aligned}11 & -13 & -16 \\ -2 & 4 & 4 \\ -5 & 7 & 10\end{aligned}].
$$

*Step 4:*

$$
{C}^{T}=[\begin{aligned}11 & -2 & -5 \\ -13 & 4 & 7 \\ -16 & 4 & 10\end{aligned}].
$$

*Step 5:*

$$
{A}^{-1}=\frac{1}{det(A)}{C}^{T}=\frac{1}{6}[\begin{aligned}11 & -2 & -5 \\ -13 & 4 & 7 \\ -16 & 4 & 10\end{aligned}].
$$

Finally, the solution to the given system is

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={A}^{-1}b \\  & =\frac{1}{6}[\begin{aligned}11 & -2 & -5 \\ -13 & 4 & 7 \\ -16 & 4 & 10\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{6}[\begin{aligned}24 \\ -24 \\ -30\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -4 \\ -5\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, $x+y+z=4-4-5=-5.$
